## Rejection Sampling

**First, review.** For $\theta \sim f(\theta)$, we want to estimate
$$I = \int a(\theta)\, f(\theta)\, d\theta$$
by the Monte Carlo method:
$$\hat I = \sum_{i=1}^N a(\theta_i) / N$$

**Overall acceptance rate:**
$$\text{Overall Acceptance Rate} = \frac{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} g(x)\,dx}$$

**Rejection Sampling 1:** choose an envelope function $g(x) \ge f(x)$ for all $x$.
```
for (i in 1:n)
  repeat
    Draw x ~ g / integral(g(x) dx)
    r = f(x) / g(x)
    Draw U ~ Unif(0, 1)
    if (U < f(x)/g(x))  x is accepted
```

![](Lec%2010%20Rejection%20sampling_images/p001-fig.png)

## Choice of Envelope Function

The tightness of the envelope function determines the efficiency of rejection sampling: a looser envelope $g_1(x)$ wastes more proposals than a tighter one $g_2(x)$ that hugs $f(x)$ more closely.

$$\text{Overall Acceptance} = \frac{\int f(x)}{\int g(x)}$$

![](Lec%2010%20Rejection%20sampling_images/p002-fig.png)

## Theorem

**Theorem:** Suppose $f$ is a function $f(x) \ge 0$ with $\int f(x)\,dx < \infty$. If $(X,V) \sim \text{Unif}(\Omega)$ where
$$\Omega = \{(x,v) \mid 0 < v < f(x)\}$$
then the PDF of $X$ is
$$\frac{f(x)}{\int f(x)\,dx}$$

Equivalently, if $X \sim g(x)$ and $V \mid X \sim \text{Unif}[0, g(x)]$, then $(X,V) \sim \text{Unif}(G)$ where $G = \{(x,v) \mid 0<v<g(x)\}$. If we further restrict to $(X,V) \in \Omega = \{(x,v) \mid 0<v<f(x)\}$, we obtain $X$ with the density above.

![](Lec%2010%20Rejection%20sampling_images/p003-fig.png)

## Proof of the Theorem

The joint PDF of $(X,V)$ is
$$P(x,v) = \frac{1}{\text{area}(\Omega)}\, I(0<v<f(x)) = \frac{1}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx} \times I(0<v<f(x))$$

Then
$$P(x) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} P(x,v)\,dv = \int_0^{+\infty} P(x,v)\,dv = \int_0^{f(x)} \frac{1}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx}\,dv$$

$$= \frac{1}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx} \cdot \int_0^{f(x)} dv = \frac{f(x)}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx}$$

## Rejection Sampling: Alternative Description

Repeat $n$ times:

1. Draw $X \sim g(x)$
2. Draw $V \sim \text{Unif}(0, g(X))$

   $\left[ V = U \cdot g(X),\quad U \sim \text{Unif}(0,1) \right]$
3. If $(V < f(X))$ accept $X$

   $V = U \cdot g(X) < f(X) \iff U < \dfrac{f(X)}{g(X)}$

   else, go back to 1)

In steps 1) and 2) we draw $(X,V) \sim \text{Unif}(G)$ where $G = \{(x,v) \mid v < g(x)\}$.

In step 3) we choose $(X,V) \in \Omega = \{(x,v) \mid v < f(x)\}$.

## Rejection Sampling (Alternative Description), Continued

**Step 1.** Draw $(X,V) \sim \text{Unif}(G)$, $G = \{(x,v) \mid 0 < v < g(x)\}$ — points fill the whole region under $g(x)$.

**Step 2.** Keep only $(X,V) \sim \text{Unif}(\Omega)$, $\Omega = \{(x,v) \mid 0 < v < f(x)\}$ — i.e., keep only the points that also fall under $f(x)$.

![](Lec%2010%20Rejection%20sampling_images/p006-fig.png)

## Example 1: Uniform Envelope

Repeat $n$ times. Let
$$f(x) = 2\, I(0 \le x \le \tfrac12), \qquad g(x) = 2\, I(0 \le x \le 1)$$

**Steps:**

1. $X \sim \text{Unif}(0,1)$
2. $V \sim \text{Unif}(0,1)$
3. $r = f(X)/g(X)$; if $(V < r)$ accept $X$, otherwise reject and go back to step 1)

In step 3), $r = f/g = \begin{cases} 1 & x < \tfrac12 \\ 0 & x > \tfrac12 \end{cases}$, so step 3) can be rewritten as:

**3\*)** If $(X < \tfrac12)$ accept $X$; otherwise go back to step 1).

Overall accept rate $= \dfrac{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} g(x)\,dx} = \dfrac12$.

![](Lec%2010%20Rejection%20sampling_images/p007-fig.png)

## Example 2

Let $\varphi(x)$ be a density (e.g. the standard normal), and define the truncated density
$$f(x) = \varphi(x)\, I(\mu \le x \le \ell)$$
so that $X \sim f(x) = \varphi(x)\, I(\mu \le x \le \ell)$.

**Repeat $n$ times:**

1. Draw $X \sim \varphi(x)$
2. If $X \in (\mu,\ell)$, accept $X$; otherwise go back to 1)

$$\text{Overall accept rate} = \frac{\int_\mu^\ell f(x)\,dx}{\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \varphi(x)\,dx} = \int_\mu^\ell f(x)\,dx = P(\mu \le X \le \ell)$$

![](Lec%2010%20Rejection%20sampling_images/p008-fig.png)

## Adaptive Rejection Sampling (ARS)

For log-concave $f(x)$ (i.e., $\log f(x)$ is concave), we can build a piecewise-linear **majorant** of $\log f(x)$ from tangent lines $\ell_1(x)$, $\ell_2(x)$, ... on partition intervals $I_1, I_2, \dots$ of the domain, where
$$g(x) = \begin{cases} e^{\ell_1(x)} & x \in I_1 \\ e^{\ell_2(x)} & x \in I_2 \end{cases}, \qquad \log g(x) = \begin{cases} \ell_1(x) & x \in I_1 \\ \ell_2(x) & x \in I_2 \end{cases}$$

Since $g(x) \ge f(x)$ everywhere, $g$ is a valid envelope for rejection sampling. Moreover
$$F_g(x) = \int_{-\infty}^x g(t)\,dt$$
has closed form, so we can sample from $g$ directly using the inverse CDF:
$$F_g(x) = \int_{-\infty}^x g(t)\,dt = \int_{-\infty}^x e^{a+bt}\,dt$$

![](Lec%2010%20Rejection%20sampling_images/p009-fig.png)

## Adaptive Rejection Sampling: Refining the Envelope

As rejected points reveal more information about $\log f(x)$, additional tangent lines are added, refining the piecewise-linear majorant $\ell(x) = \log f(x)$ over successive iterations (superscripts denote the iteration at which each piece $\ell_1^{(1)}(x), \ell_2^{(1)}(x), \ell_1^{(2)}(x), \dots$ was added), giving envelopes
$$g_1(x) = e^{\ell_1^{(1)}(x)}, \qquad g_2(x) = e^{\ell_2^{(1)}(x)}, \ \dots$$
that hug $\log f(x)$ ever more tightly, improving the acceptance rate.

![](Lec%2010%20Rejection%20sampling_images/p010-fig.png)

## Example: Truncated Normal

**Truncated Normal.**
$$f(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\, e^{-\frac{x^2}{2}}\, I(u < x < \ell)$$
$$\log f(x) = -\tfrac12 \log(2\pi) - \frac{x^2}{2}, \quad \text{for } \ell < x < u$$

A single tangent line at $\frac{u+\ell}{2}$ gives an upper bound $\ell(x) \ge \log f(x)$ on $(\ell, u)$, exponentiating to an envelope $g_1(x) = e^{\ell(x)}$ that stays above $f(x)$ on the whole truncation interval, which can be used to compute/sample $P(\ell < Z < u)$.

![](Lec%2010%20Rejection%20sampling_images/p011-fig.png)
